hoeschec wrote: NZD-USD Scalp

Hi AK,

Good questions! Price sometimes bounces from the mouth of a FL, and sometimes it bounces from the MPL of a FL. Often, price will bounce at both of these places.

Just because price bounces at the mouth doesn't necessarily mean we won't get a reaction from its MPL...in fact, I have noticed that a S/R (mouth) bounce frequently precedes a much larger bounce @ the FL's MPL. In these scenarios, the S/R (mouth) reaction sets up a supply/demand zone..acting as a 'trap' for traders who buy/sell the breakout.

Just a quick reminder to traders when it comes to drawing FL's. There are often multiple scales with different boxes. Quite frequently there are tiny low TF scale FL's that occur but aren't visible in your other time frames.

It is really easy to overlook these tiny FL's (I have a bad habit of doing it), but properly drawing them gives you a HUGE edge on the market. I recently went back through my losing trades to see what I did wrong. More than 50% of my losses were due to sloppy HTF drawing if FL's. It is amazing actually when you start practicing because you see how relevant those tiny FL's are.

Some practice on USD- CHF:

HTF (30-min chart)

Then.. I went deeper in to the 1-min chart to see why price bounced where it did.. Here is what I came up with:

Something I have been thinking about: the flag that forms after an ignored level is important...because when that new flag itself gets engulfed, and price is falling/rising from making a new reaction point (supply/demand created) the new FL formed is very reactive. This USD-CHF is a perfect example of this. Price reacts right at the lower edge of the FL.. and it went a long time.

This could have resulted in a 20:R trade if kept your SL tight; behind the green FL Box.

The question is what kind of engulf will make a real PA? Please see below diagram#1，everything I drew below are the price structure visible on H4. Price engulfed FL-D, I think we can all agree that we have PA for long at the lower FL B.

Now see diagram #2, what if we look into 1 min chart, and we saw a small kink (E) that's created after price engulfed FL-C, and this kink is located above FL-D, and while price engulf FL-D, it hit this LTF kink and then reverse downwards. Immediately, two questions jump out in my head: 1) Which FL is more important, FL-D visible on H4 timeframe, or FL-E visible on 1-min timeframe? 2) Do we still have PA for long at FL-B?

Depending on where we are going with this discussion, I would add more follow up drawings to illustrate different scenarios.

My answer is it depends on the importance of E:

If zone E is what the MPL of D reacted off of to form zone D. Then, we don't have an engulf / trade. If zone E is just a hiccup between the HTF zones, I think D is engulfed and I'm looking for a trade. If zone E was the actual FL formed right after the break of C and zone D is really more of a DBD decision point, I'm not looking for a trade because we have hit the next target.

Hi Rinehart, thank you so much for sharing man! Point 1 and point 3 are crystal clear explanation. On point 2, what do you mean by a 'hiccup', is there a difference between a hiccup and a kink?

When I drew E, I actually want E to be the LTF FL that is created immediately after the break of FL-C of H4 timeframe. But E cannot be visible of H4, it's only visible on M1. Therefore, those who did not bother to go down to M1, would not have spot it, and would only see FL-D as the FL created after the break of C.

So here is something that I am still wondering about, when a HTF barrier is broken (let's say it's an obvious weekly support level), creating a small FL that's only visible on 1-min chart, what do we call this FL? Is this a 1-min FL or a weekly FL?

Thanks again Rinehart, you are always here for us!
